summary: Usage Insights CSV export shows duplicate rows due to model aliases/version bucketing
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports that Usage Insights CSV export contains duplicate rows that appear to represent the same model, which causes Finance to double count when pivoting by (route, model).

Customer report (HelioChat)
- “Exported CSV has repeated model rows. In the console table it looks fine, but the CSV has two lines for llama-3.1-70b on the same route/time bucket.”
- They are ingesting exports into a weekly chargeback workbook and keying on (route, model, day).

Impact
- Medium customer impact: inaccurate reporting unless deduped.
- Potential billing trust issue (customer asked whether invoice totals are wrong).

Where observed
- Redwood Console → Usage/Cost → Usage Insights (beta) → Export CSV
- Time range: Last 7 days
- Filters: Project = production workspace, Group by Route + Model

Expected
- One row per (time_bucket, route, canonical model bucket) with stable model identifier.

Actual
- Two rows emitted for the same effective model bucket when the dataset contains a mix of canonical model id and alias name.

Example (sanitized)
- Columns: day, route, model, model_family, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd

Row A:
- 2026-02-05, /v1/chat/completions, llama-3.1-70b, llama-3.1, 70b, 1,240,000, 1,510,000, 482.13

Row B:
- 2026-02-05, /v1/chat/completions, llama-3.1-70b-instruct, llama-3.1, 70b, 96,000, 122,000, 39.11

Customer expectation is that the export should roll these into a single “llama-3.1-70b (70b)” bucket or, at minimum, include a stable canonical model id they can key off.

Notes
- Invoice total still matches when summing all rows; issue is duplicate grouping key for customer-side analysis.

---

Timeline / activity

2026-02-07 09:18 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Ticket created
- Acknowledged customer report and requested:
  - export file name / job id
  - screenshot of the duplicate rows
  - whether they are using any aliases/pinned model names in their SDK config

2026-02-07 11:02 PT — HelioChat (Customer) — Comment
- Provided export job id: exp_01JMQH7F8R2K3Z9 (from console toast)
- Confirmed they pin “llama-3.1-70b” in some services and “llama-3.1-70b-instruct” in others (older config).

2026-02-07 12:10 PT — Evan Scott (Solutions Eng) — Comment
- Reproduced in internal beta workspace by generating traffic with two model names that resolve to the same underlying family/version bucket.
- Confirmed console UI table appears deduped when viewing “Model family” grouping, but CSV export “Model” grouping emits both model strings.

2026-02-07 13:26 PT — Nadia Rahman (Cost attribution) — Investigation note
- Export uses the query service response grouped by `model_display_name` + `model_family` + `model_version`.
- Alias mapping currently happens at request routing but is not consistently applied in telemetry for historical events; some events carry alias, others canonical.
- Result: same bucket (family/version) appears as two groups if display name differs.

2026-02-07 14:05 PT — Cole Summers (Billing) — Comment
- Confirmed billing hooks compute cost by canonical internal `model_sku` and should reconcile; this is a reporting key issue, not a billing amount issue.
- Recommended we ensure export includes canonical key and/or forces alias normalization.

2026-02-08 10:12 PT — Evan Scott — Customer update
- Explained root cause at a high level (alias names treated as separate group keys in export).
- Confirmed invoice is not impacted.
- Provided workaround options (see below).

2026-02-09 15:40 PT — Chloe Martin (Console backend) — Engineering note
- Proposed fix:
  1) Ensure query/export grouping uses `canonical_model_id` (or `model_sku`) as the primary key.
  2) Add `canonical_model` column to export output.
  3) Derive a stable `model_bucket` label (e.g., “llama-3.1 / 70b”) for display.
- Added to backlog under model family/version bucketing work; needs careful handling for deprecated models and custom aliases.

2026-02-10 09:05 PT — Dev Patel — Resolution note + close
- Customer confirmed workaround unblocks their weekly finance report.

---

Root cause
- The export “Group by Model” path keys off model display name, which can be an alias (customer-specified) or canonical name depending on emitter/instrumentation path.
- When the same underlying model bucket is used under multiple names within the same time range, the export outputs multiple rows.

Workaround (communicated to customer)
1) Prefer grouping by Model family/version in the export workflow (instead of Model name) for chargeback reporting.
2) If they must group by model string, dedupe client-side by using (model_family, model_version, route, day) rather than (model, route, day).
3) Operationally: standardize on a single pinned model name across services (choose either canonical or alias) to avoid mixed telemetry labels.

Planned fix (product/engineering)
- Add a stable canonical identifier in exports and switch grouping key to canonical.
- ETA communicated: targeted for the next beta patch once model alias/version bucketing changes land (no guaranteed date provided; customer asked to be notified).

Customer communication summary
- Confirmed billing totals are correct; issue affects CSV grouping keys.
- Provided immediate workaround and offered to review their workbook dedupe logic if needed.

Follow-ups / next steps (internal)
- Create/track engineering work item: “Export: include canonical_model_id + group by canonical key” (to be linked once filed).
- Add regression test fixture: mixed alias + canonical events in same bucket should not produce duplicated export groups.
- Consider adding a tooltip/help doc note: “Model name may reflect alias; use Model family/version for stable reporting” (DevEx/docs).
